technical_and_design_decisions: The software increment will be implemented as a modification to an existing Spring-based project, assuming the codebase already exists and uses modern Spring Boot practices.
The core technical decisions are guided by the Spring Framework and Spring Integration upgrade path and the existing architecture implied by terms like 'DSL', 'XML generation', and 'YARN SPI'.

For the SpEL expression enhancement (U5), the design decision is to modify the existing DSL parsing or compilation phase to detect and evaluate inline SpEL expressions against the payload at the defined point.

The admin artifact split (U8) will be implemented by creating a new Maven/Gradle module (e.g., 'admin-api' or 'admin-spi') and moving the Hadoop-version-specific implementations into separate, optional modules, keeping a core interface clean of those dependencies.
Testing strategy will include unit tests for new/refactored logic, integration tests for DSL/XML variants (U4), and end-to-end validation for key user stories.
assumptions: The developer has full access to and understanding of the existing source code repository, build system (Maven/Gradle), and project structure.
The project is currently on a version of Spring Integration prior to 4.2.1, and the upgrade (U2) is a minor version bump without breaking API changes, though integration testing is required.
The '{{timeout}}' and '{{pollInterval}}' parameters (U1) are global configuration properties that will be added to a central configuration class or DSL definition object.
The 'job orchestration documentation' (U6) is a separate Markdown or HTML file within the project's documentation module, and no code changes are required, only documentation authoring and review.
The 'YARN SPI' (U7) refers to a set of interfaces and possibly an implementation for YARN integration, and the status is an enum or constant within that module.
The refactoring of 'JobLaunchingTasklet' (U3) is a performance-focused code review and rewrite, not a feature change, and will maintain the same public API contract.
The developer is proficient in Java, the Spring ecosystem, and the specific domain of batch processing and application deployment implied by the user stories.
A basic continuous integration (CI) pipeline is in place for running tests automatically.

activities.activity_description: Add `timeout` and `pollInterval` as configurable global options in the DSL configuration. Modify the relevant configuration classes and the DSL parser/compiler to recognize and propagate these values. Include unit tests for the new configuration properties and their default behavior.

Update the project's dependency management (e.g., Maven POM or Gradle build file) to use Spring Integration 4.2.1. Review the upgrade guide for breaking changes. Perform a system-wide build and test to ensure compatibility. Fix any compilation errors or deprecated usage.

Conduct a thorough code review of `JobLaunchingTasklet`. Identify performance bottlenecks (e.g., unnecessary object creation, inefficient I/O, synchronization issues). Redesign and implement the refactored logic, ensuring backward compatibility. Add performance-focused unit tests.

Analyze existing tests for DSL parsing and XML generation. Identify gaps in coverage for different combinations of modules and options. Design and implement new integration test scenarios (e.g., various DSL configurations, XML export/import variants). Execute the full test suite and resolve any failures.

activities.activity_name: Implement Inline SpEL in Stream Definition (U5)
activities.activity_description: Modify the stream definition parser/DSL compiler to detect and correctly parse inline SpEL expressions within the stream definition syntax. Integrate a SpEL evaluation step at the appropriate point in the payload processing pipeline. Ensure seamless interaction with existing operators and custom modules. Write tests for various expression types.

Draft the documentation for job orchestration, covering concepts, workflow building guidelines, and examples. Structure it logically for users. Have it reviewed by a technical writer or peer. Publish it to the appropriate documentation location (e.g., docs site, wiki, or README).

Locate the status enum or constant definition within the YARN SPI module. Add a new `UNDEPLOYED` status. Update all state transition logic and status checks to handle this new state correctly. Add unit tests to cover the new status and its transitions.

Analyze the 'admin' artifact's dependencies on Hadoop distribution-specific libraries. Define a core 'admin-api' module containing only interfaces and common logic. Create separate, optional modules for each Hadoop distribution's implementation. Refactor the original artifact to become a thin aggregator or provide a default implementation. Update build scripts and dependency declarations.
